subject.title: Add Herdr state bridge for OpenClaw TUI

question: Should Herdr pane-state reporting be accepted as bundled plugin-owned behavior gated by plugin policy, or as explicit core-owned TUI behavior outside the plugin system?
rationale: The patch mixes a bundled plugin manifest with a core `HERDR_PANE_ID` startup hook, so automation cannot choose the permanent ownership boundary safely.

options.title: Gate it as a bundled plugin
options.body: Keep the plugin package but start the sidecar only after resolved plugin policy allows `herdr-state`, including global disable, allowlist, denylist, and per-plugin disablement.

options.title: Make it core-owned
options.body: Remove the no-op plugin wrapper and document Herdr as an explicit TUI environment integration with maintainer-approved env controls.

options.title: Move it outside core
options.body: Pause or close this PR unless a generic TUI status seam is needed for external Herdr packaging.

recommendation.title: Gate it as a bundled plugin
recommendation.body: Keep the plugin package but start the sidecar only after resolved plugin policy allows `herdr-state`, including global disable, allowlist, denylist, and per-plugin disablement.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved question is product/API ownership across TUI behavior and plugin policy, and steipete has adjacent history in both surfaces.
